paragraphs: "That's funny," I tell him. "That's almost the same thing the people of Olmnar told me. Before I burned their city to the ground."
After I say that, there's a long pause in which none of us says anything.

"You're bluffing," the mage says.

"I guess there's only one way to find out, then," I tell him, as I feel my heart pounding in my chest.

The few seconds of silence that followed felt like the longest seconds in my life. After a long pause, the mage says, finally:

"You're in luck, stillwater. I'm feeling merciful today. I'm going to be out of your hair just as soon as I finish this guy here."

"You do that and you'll regret it," I say without thinking.

My last sentence seems to have taken him aback.

"What, are you kidding me? You're going to defend this lowlife?"

"If I have to. Do I have to?"
